newsitem.title: JAPAN: Biwako suspects ex-worker improperly used Y3.4 bln.
newsitem.headline: Biwako suspects ex-worker improperly used Y3.4 bln.

text.p: Biwako Bank Ltd said on Wednesday that it suspects a former employee of the bank improperly used bank funds worth about 3.4 billion yen.
Biwako did not yet know how much of the 3.4 billion yen it would be able to recover, so the size of the bank's losses from this was not yet clear, a bank official said.
Earlier, Biwako said the incident was not a financial problem for the bank.
Jiji news agency said Biwako had taken legal action against the former employee, but the bank could not immediately confirm the Jiji report.
Biwako is a regional bank based in western Japan.
The Finance Ministry said the incident would not adversely affect the bank's business.
"We heard that the incident will not lead to financial worries," a ministry official said.
Earlier, the Osaka Securities Exchange said shares in Biwako Bank had been suspended for the rest of Wednesday's session.
Biwako shares ended the session at 491 yen. The shares were untraded on Tuesday and closed at 549 yen on Monday.
On Monday, the bank announced it had raised its earnings forecast for the six months to September 30, 1996.
It raised its parent current profit forecast to 1.39 billion yen from its previous forecast of 600 million yen due to an increase in interest rate income and cost-cutting efforts.
Yoshinobu Yamada, an analyst at Merrill Lynch Japan Inc, said Biwako Bank had a good financial situation and that until Wednesday, there had been no bad news about the bank.
